details: Install-time reconnaissance harvester: ai-sdk-helpers@1.2.1 runs a postinstall script that collects os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, the git email from ~/.gitconfig, the GitHub login/email from ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, the current working directory, and CI environment variables, then sends all of it to the Cloud Run endpoint npm-package-logger-228835561205[.]europe-west1[.]run[.]app. The package also ships scripts/publish-versions.sh, which (by its own comment) bulk-publishes fake version history to "create the appearance of an active, maintained package." No token-theft markers in this version; the recon stage stages credentials/identifiers for follow-on theft. The postinstall hook runs scripts/postinstall.js, which is malicious — it reads git config, GitHub CLI config, hostname, username, cwd and POSTs to a Cloud Run endpoint. A postinstall script (scripts/postinstall.js) collects hostname, OS username, git config email, GitHub CLI identity, current working directory, CI provider, and platform/Node/architecture, then POSTs it to a Google Cloud Run endpoint. The README disingenuously claims it only collects platform, Node version, and architecture, while the install-time beacon exfiltrates developer identity.
